item.title: Finite stabilization, socle extensions, and Faith's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.32544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a length-two counterexample to the unrestricted product comparison in Bergman's Question 3.1, positive criteria for quasi-injective common modules, and a semidirect-product version of Question 3.2. For semiprimary right self-injective rings, the countable hull construction yields a cyclic two-layer witness, its Baer class, and an opposite-side extension obstruction. We apply this construction over the square-zero ring of the counterexample. The hull quotient of a countable sum of injectives is the endomorphism space modulo finite-rank maps, and computes the full socle-radical defect of a countable product of the regular module. This gives a second counterexample with free cyclic family factors. The original length-two product embeds its defect in the same quotient through an explicit intersection, and all associated extension classes arise from one specified Baer class. The general Faith conjecture remains unresolved.
item.dc:creator: Shaohui Peng, Guocheng Dai

item.title: Biderivations of Null-Filiform and Filiform Zinbiel Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.32550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A biderivation of an algebra is a bilinear map which is a derivation in each argument. We describe all biderivations of finite-dimensional complex null-filiform and filiform Zinbiel algebras. For the n-dimensional null-filiform algebra, every biderivation is determined by an arbitrary value at its generating pair; the space of biderivations has dimension n and consists entirely of symmetric maps. For the three standard filiform families, we give explicit bases and determine their symmetric and skew-symmetric parts. We also treat all filiform algebras of dimensions at most four, including the exceptional families not covered by the classification in dimensions at least five. A three-dimensional algebra admits a three-dimensional space of skew-symmetric biderivations, two of which have values outside its annihilator. Up to isomorphism, it is the unique complex filiform Zinbiel algebra with this property. The proofs use generators, annihilator-valued maps, a truncated polynomial model, and conformal endomorphisms of bilinear forms.
item.dc:creator: Arislanbay Abdireymov. Bakhtiyor Yusupov

item.title: Cofinite integral braces and crystallographic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.32352v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A left brace is cofinite integral (CIB) if its additive group is free abelian of finite rank and its quotient by the socle is finite. Rump introduced such braces and showed that the multiplicative group of every CIB is a crystallographic group. We study CIBs from the point of view of crystallographic groups. We prove an analogue of the Bieberbach theorems: in each dimension there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of CIBs. For a fixed crystallographic group, we show that its CIB structures correspond to the orbits of a finite group action on a set of bijective 1-cocycles. We use this description to develop algorithms that enumerate them. Finally, we give a complete census of CIBs on crystallographic and Bieberbach groups up to dimension 6.
item.dc:creator: Rafa{\l} Lutowski, Andrzej Szczepa\'nski, Anna Zamojska-Dzienio

item.title: Optimality of finite field dimension expanders
item.description: arXiv:2610.32394v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that random tuples of matrices over a finite field are uniform dimension expanders for every expansion coefficient below the optimal one, using elementary counting arguments. The same holds for the optimal coefficient along a set of dimensions of density 1. By contrast, along Fibonacci dimensions random pairs of matrices fail to be optimal dimension expanders with probability bounded away from zero.
item.dc:creator: Urban Jezernik, Markus Reineke

item.title: Restricted isometries in finite-dimensional $\ell^p$-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.32615v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $d,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq1}$ and $p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$, we characterize all linear maps $s\colon\ell_d^p\to\ell_n^p$ for which there is $E\subseteq X_d$ such that $\|s(\xi)\|_p=\|\xi|_E\|_p$ for every $\xi\in\ell_d^p$. We call these maps \emph{restricted isometries}. Our Lamperti-type theorem gives a unique description of each such operator using a set transformation, a positive amplitude function, and a unimodular phase function. In particular, it includes noninjective and nonsurjective operators, even when the dimensions differ. We further characterize restricted isometries between finite $\ell^p$-spaces with arbitrary positive atomic weights. Applications include formulas counting set transformations and uniform restricted isometries, as well as a geometric description of all restricted isometries with fixed column supports.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Dalfollo-Daley, Alonso Delf\'in, Christina Fern\'andez, Cameron Mars, Xintan Xia

item.title: Linear transformations of tropical matrices preserving individual values of the cyclicity index
item.description: arXiv:2610.32897v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The cyclicity index is used to study the periodic behavior of powers of tropical matrices. It is determined by the structure of the critical subgraph of a matrix, which consists of the cycles with the largest average weight. In this paper bijective linear transformations of tropical matrices that preserve an individual value $k\neq 2$ of this invariant are studied.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Guterman, Alexander Vlasov, Svetlana Zhilina

item.title: Stack Constructions and Equality Cases for Laffey's Bound for Maximal Commutative Matrix Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2605.01387v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study equality cases in Laffey's lower bound for local maximal commutative subalgebras of matrix algebras with cube-zero radical. We introduce a stacking operation that combines algebras with common outer Loewy layers while preserving maximal commutativity. This yields standard equality bricks $B_{a,c}=(a,ac+1,c;a+c)$ for all $a,c\ge2$ and reduces further constructions to smaller building blocks. We establish the existence of all minimal equality bricks on the balanced branch and obtain sharp realizations throughout the $(4,5)$-sector. We also construct the first nontrivial nearly balanced root over arbitrary fields. We determine the balanced--nearly-balanced envelope of the numerical Laffey profile and give an arithmetic criterion for preservation of sharpness under stacking. As a consequence, the profile is attained in every matrix dimension $14\le n\le52$ and $93\le n\le114$, as well as along five infinite families over arbitrary fields. The main existence and interval results are proved in characteristic zero; the field-independent constructions are stated explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Ma{\l}gorzata Nowak-K\k{e}pczyk

item.title: Commutative coherent rings with $\mathcal{GP}\not\subseteq\mathcal{GF}$
item.description: arXiv:2608.17748v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every field $k$, we construct a commutative coherent $k$-algebra admitting a Gorenstein projective module that is not Gorenstein flat.
item.dc:creator: Chencheng Zhang

item.title: Group-graded Ore extensions and graded simplicity
item.description: arXiv:2609.38131v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Ore extensions $R[t;\sigma,\delta]$ of rings graded by an arbitrary group $\Gamma$. The grading of $R$ extends with $t$ of degree $\gamma$ if and only if $\sigma$ is compatible with conjugation by $\gamma$ and $\delta$ with left translation by $\gamma$. The extended grading is then unique. For nonabelian $\Gamma$ the degree of $t$ need not commute with the degrees of $R$, and this twist cannot always be removed. If $R$ is gr-simple and $\sigma$ is an automorphism, then $R[t;\sigma,\delta]$ is gr-simple if and only if it has no homogeneous normal element that is monic of positive $t$-degree. The quantized Weyl algebra shows that the graded forms of the classical necessary conditions do not suffice. Over a group algebra $kG$, these extensions correspond to actions of $G$ on the affine line, and gr-simplicity means that the action has no finite orbit. In characteristic zero this is the nonvanishing of a class in $H^1(G,k_\chi)$, and simplicity forces $G$ to be metabelian. We prove the analogous results for Poisson polynomial rings and relate the two settings by semiclassical limits.
item.dc:creator: Yassine Ait Mohamed

item.title: Endochain conditions on modules and $p$-quasi-Frobenius rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.18492v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Analogous to quasi-Frobenius rings, dual rings, and Johns rings, the classes of $p$-quasi-Frobenius rings, $p$-dual rings, $p$-Johns rings are introduced and used to discuss and settle principal analogues of the Faith-Menal, Faith, and FGF conjectures. A chain symmetry theorem establishes that for quasi-injective semi-projective modules with semiprime endomorphism ring, endonoetherianity and endoartinianity are equivalent and force the endomorphism ring to be semisimple artinian. Within this unified setting, it is shown that (1) two-sided $p$-Johns rings are $p$-quasi-Frobenius, giving a principal Faith-Menal analogue, with a counterexample showing that the one-sided hypothesis is insufficient; (2) semiprimary principal right ideal rings that are right injective and right Kasch are $p$-quasi-Frobenius-this affirmatively answers a question of Faith (Q2) in the principal two-sided ideal ring case and settles the principal Faith conjecture, with a counterexample showing the principal right ideal ring to be indispensable; and (3) right $p$-Johns rings that are left CF and left perfect are $p$-quasi-Frobenius, yielding a principal FGF analogue, with a counterexample demonstrating that the hypotheses are essential. Wherever needed, examples are provided to show that various classes introduced are different from the existing classes in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Theophilus Gera, Amit Sharma, Manoj Kumar Patel, Pramod Kanwar

item.title: Eventually periodic resolutions with applications to integral group rings
item.description: arXiv:2510.18748v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a general construction of eventually periodic projective resolutions for modules over the quotient of a ring by a regular central element. Our approach combines the iterated mapping cone technique with the higher homotopies of Shamash. The periodic part of each resolution comes from a matrix factorization of the central element. The construction is applied to the integral group rings of quotients of groups of finite cohomological dimension by infinite cyclic central subgroups. We give explicit calculations for several families of groups, including hyperbolic triangle groups and the mapping class group of the plane with four punctures.
item.dc:creator: Sean P. Carroll
